findings.summary: The spec-governed request-consumption defect from the prior final review (rf-942a12b6) is fixed: _run_call (kernel_coordinator.py:264-276) now calls abort_unavailable_call (request_kernel.py:945-977) when the Goal-call port is unbound, recording RECORD_CALL_UNAVAILABLE, releasing the fence, and re-queueing the request at its original head without persisting a Stop List or call_result; restore() (request_kernel.py:671-683) keeps the request pending. The offline regression TestUnboundGoalCallPreservesRequests (tests/test_goal_request_kernel.py:1334-1381) accepts multiple requests with no port, reconstructs, binds a fake port, and asserts once-in-order delivery. compileall exit 0 and 57/57 kernel tests pass per the implement handoff verification record.

Goal version activation is not wired into the production composition path: build_line (runner.py:227-232) constructs GoalRequestKernel without calling activate_version, so active_version stays empty until a live version event; the version-bound approve/reject refusal is correctly implemented and offline-tested against an explicit active_version (test_stale_version_approval). This deferral is consistent with the spec's explicitly deferred later slices (full enroll/repo lifecycle and live binding), not a development-stage violation.
